claims.text: Local chemical disorder, quantified by mixing entropy, governs the superconducting transition temperature in HEA superconductors.
Higher random elemental mixing enhances electron scattering.
Disorder-enhanced scattering weakens electron–phonon coupling.
High local chemical disorder acts as a pair breaker and lowers Tc relative to a locally ordered state.
A (TaNb)1−x(HfZrTi)x type-A HEA can have a bcc structure and Tc around 7–7.8 K.
Conventional melting produces a fully random elemental distribution in the baseline alloy.
Mild annealing below the phase-separation regime can promote partial chemical ordering while preserving the overall composition.
A minor compositional adjustment can lower mixing entropy without altering the overall electron count.
The relevant structural mediator is the size and distribution of chemically ordered microdomains within an otherwise single-phase bcc solid solution.
Electron count and degree of disorder are parameters that can affect superconductivity in these HEA families.
Increasing configurational disorder increases scattering centers for Cooper pairs.
Reducing local disorder facilitates more coherent electron pairing and raises Tc.
Samples processed to reduce local disorder will have a higher Tc than the high-disorder baseline.
Samples processed to reduce local disorder may have a higher upper critical field Hc2.
The proposed disorder control applies when electron count and the single-phase bcc crystal structure remain constant.
The proposed mechanism is limited to conventional BCS superconductors outside regimes dominated by Anderson localization or unconventional effects.
The quantitative relationship between mixing entropy and Tc is not established.
The magnitude of a Tc change may depend on disorder, electron count, and lattice stability.
Tc and Hc2 can be characterized under cryogenic, field-dependent conditions using SQUID magnetometry.
A controlled comparison can use identically composed rapidly quenched and mildly annealed samples, with local order and superconducting properties measured under identical conditions.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis treats mixing entropy as the quantitative measure of local disorder, but the decisive comparison holds overall composition fixed. The cited ideal mixing-entropy expression depends only on elemental fractions, so annealing identically composed samples would not change that stated ΔSmix even if it changed short-range order. A separate local-order parameter is therefore required.

An Hc2 increase is described only as possible, yet the falsification rule invokes failure to increase Tc 'or Hc2.' Absence of an optional Hc2 increase cannot by itself falsify the stated Tc-centered mechanism.
